proposals.hypothesis: NASICON-type LiTi2(PO4)3 is known for Li-ion conductivity and may exhibit stability and insulating properties suitable for coating.
LiAlSiO4 silicate may offer good chemical stability and moderate Li-ion transport, with potential compatibility with oxide electrolytes.
Li3BO3 borate could provide stable interfacial layer due to boron's ability to form glassy phases, potentially insulating with adequate band gap.
Simple halide LiF has high band gap and may act as stable insulating layer, though Li-ion conductivity may be limited.
LiTaO3 oxide with high dielectric constant and wide band gap may offer electrochemical stability and insulation at 4V.
Li2ZrO3 contains Zr present in the LLZO electrolyte, potentially enhancing interfacial compatibility and stability.
Complex fluoride LiCaAlF6 may combine high voltage stability of fluorides with improved Li-ion conduction from structural complexity.
LiTaF6 fluoride with Ta in high oxidation state may offer stability against oxidation at high voltage and adequate insulation.
LiAlO2 oxide is known as a stable ceramic with wide band gap, potentially suitable as inert coating layer.
Oxyfluoride Li2NbOF5 may combine oxide stability with fluorine's electronegativity for improved interfacial resistance reduction.
